clips.text: You've got money in your TEETH!
clips.script: [amazed, loud] You've got money in your TEETH!

clips.text: Mr. Washington, there's a notice taped to your roses in there.
clips.script: [noticing, careful] Mr. Washington, there's a notice taped to your roses in there.

clips.text: Through the dog door. Nara's never once used the dog door.
clips.script: [mellow, wondering] through the dog door. [mellow, laid-back, low-key, dry, amazed] nara's never once used the dog door.

clips.text: Nine papers. There were twelve. So the one with the pan still has three.
clips.script: [counting, small teacher] Nine papers. There were twelve. [working it out] So the one with the pan still has three.

clips.text: How many loaves?
clips.script: [gruff, businesslike] How many loaves?

clips.text: At 5:30 this morning. Before the incident. It still applies.
clips.script: [crisp, unbothered] At five thirty this morning. [firm] Before the incident. [flat, immovable] It still applies.

clips.text: And that's my good twelve-cup pan on your head. It's never been in pond water in its life.
clips.script: [warm Long Island accent, sharp, pointing] And that's my good twelve-cup pan on your head. [warm Long Island accent, offended, fast] It's never been in POND water in its life.

clips.text: Under Lamby! Nobody looks under Lamby!
clips.script: [instant, certain] Under Lamby! [stating a fact] NOBODY looks under Lamby!

clips.text: You saw a person do this?
clips.script: [intent, quiet] You saw a PERSON do this?

clips.text: Then I guess we're following a flame down the street. Bring the dough. I'm not leaving loaf thirty-one alone with the dog.
clips.script: [mellow, resigned] then i guess we're following a flame down the street. [mellow, laid-back, low-key, easy, practical] bring the dough. [mellow, laid-back, low-key, deadpan] i'm not leaving loaf thirty-one alone with the dog.

clips.text: It's grey, Rose. Just that one spot. And that orange cube has a dragonfly in it.
clips.script: [correcting, patient] It's grey, Rose. Just that one spot. [curious, slower] And that orange cube has a dragonfly in it.

clips.text: I used to do two hundred before midnight. Load me. If this is my last shift, I'm not ending it on three.
clips.script: [gruff, proud, rousing] I used to do two hundred before midnight. [commanding] Load me. [firm, dignified] If this is my last shift, I'm not ending it on THREE.

clips.text: The date's on it.
clips.script: [flat, final] The date's on it.

clips.text: I worked the night shift, Tom. I've walked up to worse. Mister, take off my pan.
clips.script: [warm Long Island accent, unbothered, brisk] I worked the night shift, Tom. I've walked up to worse. [warm Long Island accent, firm, to the fish] Mister, take off my pan.

clips.text: One more ride, Tata! To the cab! Go the LONG way!
clips.script: [demanding, loud] One more ride, Tata! To the cab! Go the LONG way!

clips.text: Bernadette, that's the most useful thing anyone has told me in eight of these.
clips.script: [sincere, impressed] Bernadette, that's the most useful thing anyone has told me in EIGHT of these.

clips.text: It's grape. Do you want one?
clips.script: [mellow, helpful] it's grape. [mellow, laid-back, low-key, easy, generous] do you want one?

clips.text: Tata, stop. You're getting fingerprints on it. And look, it has a dent. Did you do that?
clips.script: [bossy] Tata, stop. You're getting fingerprints on it. [noticing] And look, it has a dent. [suspicious] Did YOU do that?

clips.text: Somebody's going to stand up tonight and say they arranged this bread. Somebody always did.
clips.script: [dry, knowing] Somebody's going to stand up tonight and say they arranged this bread. [flat, weary] Somebody ALWAYS did.

clips.text: That bulb is evidence, 3468.
clips.script: [sharp, possessive] That bulb is evidence, three four six eight.
